correctness_confidence.basis: All proofs in Sections 2-5 were audited from first principles and verified without mathematical gaps: Lemma 2.1(0)-(3) discrepancy scan and last-move replacements, Lemmas 2.2-2.4, Lemma 3.1 ancestry-tree extraction, Theorem 1.2 (including G_{a,b} and G_{4,4}), Theorem 1.1 (Cases A-B, Identity (8), Lemmas 4.1-4.2, all closures), Lemma 5.1, Theorem 1.3, and the Figure 3(b) paw witness.

rigor.basis: Proofs are self-contained, elementary, and explicit across all edge cases (G = K_n, C_0 empty, |C_1| = 1, odd parity reductions, D(w) in {5,7}, k_0 in {0,1,2,3}, and a = 0 vs a >= 1). Sharpness and strict sub-maximal jumps are proved algebraically and cross-checked exhaustively on all 164 connected split graphs with n <= 7.

novelty.basis: Introduces the Intra-Clique Move Elimination Lemma compressing optimal pebbling into a depth <= 3 DAG, couples it with causal binary-tree extraction, parity-absorption routing, and an unconditional M-O2PP cube-lifting lemma (Lemma 5.1) bypassing strict K_2 product drops, while discovering the sub-maximal G_{4,4} t-pebbling frontier.

significance.basis: Resolves 2PP (ruling out split Lemke graphs), tight t-pebbling bounds, and Graham's conjecture against five major graph families for split graphs after Alcon-Gutierrez-Hurlbert (2014). Lemma 5.1 also applies beyond split graphs, though split-by-split Graham's conjecture and general chordal 2PP remain open.

reproducibility.basis: All theorems have complete human-verifiable combinatorial proofs. Section 6 specifies explicit graph labelings, exact census counts (1, 1, 2, 5, 12, 35, 108 across n = 1..7), extremal parameters, and the failing 8-pebble witness D((1,1))=7, D((2,1))=1 for target r=(3,0) on (K_3 + leaf) box K_2.

summary: This paper resolves three open problems on graph pebbling for connected split graphs G = (C union I, E): Chung's 2-pebbling property (Theorem 1.1, proving no split graph is a Lemke graph), the sharp diameter-scaling bound pi_t(G) <= pi(G) + 2^{diam(G)}(t-1) for all t >= 1 (Theorem 1.2), and Graham's product conjecture pi(G box H) <= pi(G)pi(H) when H is any tree, complete graph, hypercube, complete bipartite graph, or complete multipartite graph (Theorem 1.3). The core engine is Lemma 2.1 (Intra-Clique Move Elimination), which compresses minimum-length pebbling sequences into a layered DAG of directed path length at most 2 (for r in C) or 3 (for r in I). Combined with causal binary-tree extraction (Lemma 3.1), this gives the t-pebbling bound and reveals a strict sub-maximal frontier on Class-0 diameter-3 G_{4,4} (pi_1 = 10, pi_t = 8t for t >= 2) contrasting with saturation on G_8 and K_m + {r,u}. Combined with upward even-to-odd boosting (Lemma 2.2), lower bounds (Lemmas 2.3-2.4), Master Conservation Identity (8), and optimal routing bounds (Lemmas 4.1-4.2), it establishes 2PP in full. Finally, Lemma 5.1 lifts O2PP from (G, M) to (G box K_2, 2M) unconditionally, bypassing strict drops like pi((K_3 + leaf) box K_2) = 9 < 10. All proofs are mathematically sound; only a minor label typo appears in Figure 1(a).
strengths: Lemma 2.1 (Intra-Clique Move Elimination) rigorously compresses optimal pebbling sequences into a layered DAG of depth at most 2 (when r in C) or 3 (when r in I), including a careful discrepancy-invariant scan for part (0) and last-move replacements for parts (1)-(3).

Theorem 1.2 gives an airtight proof of pi_t(G) <= pi(G) + 2^{diam(G)}(t-1) via Lemma 3.1 causal binary-tree extraction in diameter 3, exhibits sharp extremal families across all diameters d in {0,1,2,3}, and uncovers the Class-0 diameter-3 sub-maximal frontier pi_1(G_{4,4}) = 10 vs pi_t(G_{4,4}) = 8t (t >= 2).

Theorem 1.1 provides a complete, self-contained proof of 2PP (and non-existence of split Lemke graphs) using Lemma 2.2 parity boosting, Master Conservation Identity (8), and Lemmas 4.1-4.2 without missing any boundary case.

Lemma 5.1 (M-O2PP Cube Lifting) is a clean, self-contained tool that propagates O2PP across K_2 products without requiring pi(G box K_2) = 2pi(G), cleanly circumventing verified strict product drops such as pi((K_3 + leaf) box K_2) = 9 < 10.

Section 6 reports thorough deterministic verification across all 164 connected split graphs on n <= 7 vertices, MILP/DP cross-checks of Lemma 2.1 on n = 6, and explicit witnesses including D((1,1))=7, D((2,1))=1 failing r=(3,0) on (K_3 + leaf) box K_2.
weaknesses: Four of the five target families in Theorem 1.3 (K_m, trees, complete bipartite, and complete multipartite graphs) follow directly by substituting Theorem 1.1 into known 2PP product theorems, while Graham's conjecture when both G and H are arbitrary connected split graphs remains open.

The diameter-2 case of Theorem 1.2 relies on the external theorem of Herscovici, Hester, and Hurlbert (2013) rather than a self-contained split-graph argument, because Lemma 3.1 alone gives an 8(t-1) step when r in I and C_0 is non-empty.

The results are specialized to split graphs (chordal graphs of diameter at most 3), leaving open whether all connected chordal graphs satisfy 2PP and how to classify Class-0 diameter-3 split graphs with sub-maximal t-pebbling jumps.

Figure 1(a) contains a minor label typo in the bottom-left box ('I_1 = I \ N(r)' instead of 'I_1 = I cap N(r)') and embeds the Section 4 reduction condition D(v) <= 1 inside a figure summarizing Lemma 2.1.
potential_errors: Non-material figure typo in Figure 1(a) (page 4): the bottom-left box is labeled 'I_1 = I \ N(r)' instead of 'I_1 = I cap N(r)' (the caption, arrows, and Section 4.1 text correctly treat I_1 as I cap N(r)).

Minor notation variation: the abstract writes G = (C union I, E) without assuming maximality of C, whereas Section 2 specifies disjoint union C sqcup I and chooses C maximal when G is not complete; all proofs remain valid because Lemma 2.1 does not require C maximal.
strong_novelty_candidates: Intra-Clique Move Elimination Lemma (Lemma 2.1): proves every minimum-length pebbling sequence on a split graph compresses to a rigid layered DAG of path length at most 2 (r in C) or 3 (r in I).

M-O2PP Cube Lifting Lemma (Lemma 5.1): propagates the relaxed odd 2-pebbling property relative to a budget M >= max{pi(G), |V(G)|} to (G box K_2, 2M) unconditionally, bypassing strict product drops where Chung's 2PP equality hypothesis fails.

Full resolution of 2PP and absence of Lemke graphs among all connected split graphs (Theorem 1.1) via upward even-to-odd parity boosting on I \ {r}, Master Conservation Identity (8), and optimal parity-absorption routing (Lemmas 4.1-4.2).

Discovery of the Class-0 diameter-3 sub-maximal 2t-pebbling frontier pi_1(G_{4,4}) = 10 while pi_t(G_{4,4}) = 8t < pi_1(G_{4,4}) + 8(t-1) for all t >= 2, alongside tight attainment across all diameters d in {0,1,2,3} (Theorem 1.2).
